originalTitle: Players hit out at A-Leagues’ conduct over pay offer: ‘Continues to erode trust’
summary: A-League officials have been accused of negotiating in bad faith by speaking to the media within hours of their latest offer, which includes an increased women’s salary cap
content: A-League officials have been accused of negotiating in bad faith by speaking to the media within hours of their latest pay offer, as the players’ union said the conduct “continues to erode … trust”. The men’s and women’s competitions remain without a bargaining agreement two months before the start of the new season. Negotiations have stalled recently and the possibility of strike action has been raised. The Australian Professional Leagues (APL), which operates the A-Leagues, sent their latest offer to players on Wednesday, calling a late afternoon press conference at short notice soon afterwards. The offer invited players’ union Professional Footballers Australia (PFA) to come back to the table to discuss an updated position, which included an increase to the A-League Women salary cap. The new one-year, bridging deal proposed also promised to commit to “setting a pathway to full-time professionalism for ALW players, with the aim of having a mutually-agreed plan in place within 12 months”. A fully professional A-League Women competition has been one of the key goals for players in this round of bargaining, despite financial challenges at the APL and some clubs. APL chief executive, Steve Rosich, said they were committed to negotiations “in good faith” since they began eight months ago. “Our updated proposal underlines a real and genuine intent on the APL’s part to arrive at an outcome that both meets the near-term priorities in a responsible and viable way, and to turn our focus with the PFA on building meaningful and sustainable growth that will be good for everyone involved in the professional game,” he said. PFA chief executive Beau Busch issued a response on Wednesday evening, criticising the decision for the APL to go to media so soon after sharing their updated proposal. “Rather than allowing the players a reasonable opportunity to fully consider it, the APL has instead immediately announced it in the media, revealing a fundamental misunderstanding of how good faith bargaining works. “The players deserve the respect of hearing directly about proposals that affect their careers through a genuine process, rather than reading about them in the media. “The players overwhelmingly rejected the APL’s previous final offer due to a fundamental lack of trust that it would have secured the leagues’ futures after years of mismanagement. The APL’s conduct continues to erode that trust.” Rosich defended the decision to go to the media when talking with journalists on Wednesday afternoon. “We’ve been silent, obviously, in the marketplace until now, but we think now’s the right time to outline where we’re at and where we’re going,” he said. “I have spoken to Beau today, we have issued a detailed letter to Beau, he has that information. I explained we were going to articulate our position in the marketplace so the marketplace was informed – not just the players but the clubs – and we think stakeholders in our game need to know what we’re putting forward.” The A-League Men season begins on 16 October, with the women’s competition kicking off the following day.
chineseTitle: 球员们猛烈抨击澳超联赛的薪酬行为：“继续侵蚀信任”
chineseSummary: 澳超联赛官员被指控在谈判中存在恶意，他们在提出最新报价后数小时内就向媒体发表讲话，其中包括提高女性工资上限
chineseContent: 澳超联赛官员被指控在最新薪资报价后数小时内向媒体发表讲话，进行恶意谈判，球员工会表示这种行为“继续侵蚀……信任”。新赛季开始前两个月，男子和女子比赛仍没有达成谈判协议。最近谈判陷入僵局，罢工行动的可能性已经被提出。运营A联赛的澳大利亚职业联盟（APL）周三向球员发出了最新的报价，并在不久后的短时间内召开了下午晚些时候的新闻发布会。该提议邀请球员工会澳大利亚职业足球运动员（PFA）回到谈判桌讨论更新的立场，其中包括提高澳大利亚女足联赛的工资上限。新提出的为期一年的过渡协议还承诺致力于“为 ALW 球员提供一条通往全职职业化的道路，目标是在 12 个月内制定一项双方商定的计划”。尽管APL和一些俱乐部面临财务挑战，但完全职业化的A联赛女子比赛一直是球员在本轮谈判中的关键目标之一。 APL 首席执行官史蒂夫·罗西奇 (Steve Rosich) 表示，自八个月前开始谈判以来，他们一直致力于“真诚地”进行谈判。他说：“我们更新的提案强调了 APL 的真正意图，即以负责任和可行的方式达成既满足近期优先事项的结果，又将我们与 PFA 的重点转向建立有意义和可持续的增长，这对职业比赛的每个参与者都有好处。” PFA首席执行官博·布施(Beau Busch)周三晚间做出回应，批评APL在分享最新消息后这么快就向媒体公开的决定。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
